questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a solution to a pair of linear equations in two variables?
choices: A line that represents all possible solutions
An ordered pair that satisfies both equations
A single value that satisfies one equation
A graph that intersects at two points
questions.solution: The correct answer is an ordered pair that satisfies both equations, as this represents the point where the two lines intersect, fulfilling both equations simultaneously. A line that represents all possible solutions would describe a single equation, not a system. A single value that satisfies one equation does not account for both equations. A graph that intersects at two points would imply two separate solutions, which is not possible for a consistent linear system.

questions.stem: What does it mean if two lines representing a pair of linear equations intersect at a point?

questions.stem: A linear equation in two variables is given as 60x + 50y = 280, where x is the number of kilograms of mangoes and y is the number of kilograms of bananas. If Radha buys 3 kg of mangoes, how many kilograms of bananas does she buy?
questions.solution: Substitute x = 3 into the equation 60x + 50y = 280. This gives 60(3) + 50y = 280, or 180 + 50y = 280. Subtracting 180 from both sides gives 50y = 100, so y = 2. The option '3 kg' is incorrect because it assumes x and y are equal. The option '4 kg' is incorrect because it uses an incorrect calculation. The option '5 kg' is incorrect because it assumes a different value for x.

questions.stem: A pair of linear equations in two variables has a unique solution at (5, -1). One of the equations is x - y = 6. Which of the following could be the other equation?
questions.solution: The point (5, -1) must satisfy both equations. Substituting x = 5 and y = -1 into 2x - 3y = 13 gives 2(5) - 3(-1) = 10 + 3 = 13, which is correct. The other options either do not satisfy the point or are not in the correct form. The distractors may result from miscalculating the substitution or choosing equations with similar coefficients but incorrect constants.

hi.stem: दो चरों में रैखिक समीकरणों का एक युग्म (5, -1) पर एक अद्वितीय हल है। एक समीकरण x - y = 6 है। निम्न में से कौन-सा समीकरण दूसरा समीकरण हो सकता है?
hi.solution: बिंदु (5, -1) दोनों समीकरणों को संतुष्ट करना चाहिए। x = 5 और y = -1 को 2x - 3y = 13 में प्रतिस्थापित करने पर 2(5) - 3(-1) = 10 + 3 = 13, जो सही है। अन्य विकल्प या बिंदु को संतुष्ट नहीं करते हैं या सही रूप में नहीं हैं। भ्रमित करने वाले विकल्प या तो स्थानापन्न की गलत गणना के कारण हो सकते हैं या समान गुणांक लेकिन गलत अचर वाले समीकरण चुने जा सकते हैं।

The option '3x + 0y - 5 = 0' is incorrect because it incorrectly places the coefficient of x. The option '5x + 3y - 1 = 0' is incorrect because it uses the wrong coefficients. questions.stem: If the equations 10x – 5y = 20 and 4x – 2y = 8 are solved, how many solutions do they have?
questions.solution: The equations 10x – 5y = 20 and 4x – 2y = 8 are multiples of each other, meaning they represent the same line and thus have infinitely many solutions. If one equation can be obtained by multiplying the other by a constant, they are not independent and share all points on the line. The other options are incorrect because the equations are not parallel (which would mean no solution) or inconsistent (which would also mean no solution).
